summary: NASA has officially initiated plans to establish a United States Space Academy following a presidential mandate, releasing a request for information to guide the civil program's creation. In international developments, Djibouti is preparing to sign the Artemis Accords to join the U.S.-led lunar exploration framework. Commercial and military launch sectors saw significant activity as SpaceX successfully placed a classified U.S. Space Force payload into orbit from California, while U.S. Space Command conducted multi-orbit satellite maneuvering exercises and selected a site in Texas for a new deep-space radar installation targeted to be operational by 2030. Commercial contract awards saw NASA add Relativity Space’s heavy-lift Terran R rocket to its launch services portfolio and award Inversion Space a contract to study aerocapture flight, alongside TrustPoint contracting EnduroSat to build a 40-satellite navigation constellation and Tomorrow.io revealing next-generation weather instruments. In space science, planetary researchers analyzing probe data found that Mercury is shrinking faster than previously estimated, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory identified unexplained "hypersoft" X-ray sources, and an analysis of 3,000 supernovas indicated dark energy may be evolving over time. Additionally, NASA announced that the commander and pilot of the upcoming Artemis II mission have shifted to emeritus astronaut status following their active training assignments. Readers should watch for the upcoming formal signing ceremony as Djibouti officially joins the Artemis Accords.
